chunks: And in the narration of Hammad from Hariz, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

No one is kept perpetually in prison except three: the one held for a capital case, who is kept until he is executed; the woman who apostasizes from Islam; and the thief after the cutting of the hand and the foot.

key_terms.الرِّجْلِ: the foot, mentioned as part of the punishment
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief subject to the stated legal punishment
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: the religion from which apostasy is mentioned here
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: capital punishment or death penalty in context
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدَّةُ: a woman who has apostasized from Islam
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, mentioned as part of the punishment

ai.seo_question: Who may be kept in prison indefinitely according to this hadith from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning those who may remain in prison for an extended or indefinite term under specified judicial circumstances. It identifies three categories: a person detained in a murder case until execution, a woman who apostasizes from Islam, and a thief after amputation of the hand and foot.
